featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Jogeshwari Mandir, Mumbai | A Powerful Spiritual Experience with Mahadev’s Energetic Shiv Ling

Jogeshwari Mandir in Mumbai is one of those rare temples where the spiritual energy is felt instantly—quietly, deeply, and unmistakably. As a staunch Hindu believer, my visit here was not just a darshan, but a genuinely soul-stirring experience that stayed with me long after I stepped out.

🛕 First Impressions & Temple Vibration

The moment you approach the temple, there is a strong sense of sanctity and tradition. Despite being located in bustling Mumbai, the inner space feels like a spiritual cocoon—calm, devotional, and grounded. The atmosphere naturally encourages silence, prayer, and gratitude.

🔱 Special Mention: The Powerful Shiv Ling of Mahadev

The highlight of this temple for me was the Shiv Ling of Mahadev—truly powerful and radiating with an intense, divine energy. Standing in front of the Shiv Ling, you feel a deep stillness, as if the space itself is charged with devotion and centuries of faith.

For devotees of Lord Shiva, this is not a casual stop—it feels like an experience of presence. The darshan brings a sense of strength and peace simultaneously, and the energy around the sanctum is something I would describe as palpably spiritual.

🌺 Darshan Experience & Devotee Flow

Even during peak times, darshan is managed with respect and discipline. The temple maintains an orderly flow, allowing devotees enough time to connect, pray, and absorb the spiritual atmosphere without feeling rushed. The collective chants, the bells, and the devotion in the air elevate the experience further.

🧼 Cleanliness, Maintenance & Overall Comfort

The premises are well-maintained and clean, reflecting reverence for the deity and consideration for devotees. For seniors and families, the environment feels safe and manageable—an important point for those planning a spiritual visit in Mumbai.

📍 Location & Accessibility

Located in Jogeshwari, the temple is accessible for residents and visitors from Andheri, Goregaon, Malad, and other nearby areas. If you’re searching for:
•	Jogeshwari Mandir Mumbai
•	Shiv Mandir in Jogeshwari
•	Mahadev Shiv Ling darshan Mumbai
•	spiritual places in Mumbai
this temple should definitely be on your list.

🕉️ Why This Temple Stands Out

✅ Deep spiritual vibration even in a busy city
✅ Mahadev’s Shiv Ling radiating powerful energy
✅ Traditional sanctity and peaceful ambience
✅ Disciplined darshan management
✅ A true place for prayer, reflection, and inner grounding

⭐ Final Verdict

⭐ 5/5 — for the divine atmosphere, powerful darshan, and the extraordinary spiritual presence of Mahadev.

Jogeshwari Mandir is a reminder that faith is alive and deeply rooted in Mumbai. If you seek a temple where you can truly feel Mahadev’s presence, this is a must-visit.

🙏 Har Har Mahadev 🙏

featured_reviews.name: vishal sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is ancient rock cut cave temple nestled amidst the bustling narrow lanes of Jogeshwari area. The construction time of the cave temple is said to be mid first century. The carvings are not much intricate but there are imposing columnades and verandahs. The rock has been cut vertically downward as in Ellora. It represents massive human work of those days

There us Jagdamba temple in central and also Ganesh and Dattatreya temple in other niches. Ma Shakti is enshrined in foot carvings form. Ganesh is massive and vermillion coated. Dattatreya is small and etched on vertical rock surface.

Caves are under ASI protection but not maintained well and is encroached upon. It is the locality people who are doing the needful.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A truly divine and beautiful temple with a very peaceful and positive vibe. The temple is well maintained and very clean.

It follows traditional South Indian temple architecture and is located on the 3rd floor of the building.

📍 Location

Located around 1.5 km away from Chembur Railway Station. You can reach easily by auto or even by walk (I personally went by walk).

🕒 Timings
•	Morning: 6:00 AM – 12:00 PM
•	Evening: 5:00 PM – 9:00 PM
(Timings may vary during festival days)

🛕 Deities Present
•	Lord Muruga (main deity)
•	Lord Guruvayurappa
•	Durga Devi
•	Lord Ganapathi

All idols are beautifully decorated and give a strong devotional feel.

🏛 Facilities & Structure

•	Total 104 steps to climb
•	Lift facility available (convenient for elderly and differently-abled devotees)
•	A small stage area where cultural programs like Natyanjali and other functions are conducted during special occasions

Overall

A calm and spiritual South Indian temple in Chembur. Definitely worth visiting if you are looking for peace and a divine experience 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Yashasvini Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
My sister’s wedding was held at Chedda Nagar Murugan Temple Marriage Hall on 27th and 28th May. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing due to a major air-conditioning issue that persisted throughout both days of the event.

The management took some action on the first day after the issue was reported, but the problem remained unresolved and continued on the second day. This caused considerable discomfort for our guests and affected the overall experience of an important family occasion.

The food and catering arrangements were excellent, but they were arranged independently by us and are not related to the hall’s services. Our concern is specifically regarding the venue facilities and the lack of an effective resolution to the AC problem despite repeated complaints.

When families book a venue for a wedding, they expect essential facilities to function properly. Based on our experience, I would not recommend Chedda Nagar Murugan Temple Marriage Hall for either small or large functions. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves the maintenance and monitoring of its facilities for future customers.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Warty
featured_reviews.review_text:
it is a spiritual haven that offers peace, tranquility, and a deep sense of connection to the divine. Whether you are a devout follower or simply someone seeking a moment of serenity, this temple provides a beautiful and calming experience.

Serene Atmosphere:
The first thing you notice upon entering Temple is its serene and peaceful atmosphere. Nestled in the bustling area of Jogeshwari East, the temple feels like a world apart, where the noise and stress of city life melt away. The calm environment, with its soothing chants and the fragrance of incense, creates a perfect setting for prayer, meditation, and reflection.

Architectural Beauty:
The temple is beautifully designed, with traditional architecture that exudes a sense of timelessness and reverence. The intricately carved idols, the elegant temple structure, and the well-maintained surroundings all contribute to the temple’s aesthetic appeal. The sanctum sanctorum, where the main deity, Lord Shiva (Rameshwar), resides, is especially captivating, inspiring devotion and awe.

Spiritual Significance:
Temple is not just a place of worship; it’s a site of deep spiritual significance. Devotees come here to seek blessings, offer prayers, and participate in the various religious ceremonies and festivals that are regularly held. The temple is particularly vibrant during Shivratri, when it comes alive with celebrations, special prayers, and a large influx of devotees.

Welcoming Community:
The temple’s community is warm and welcoming. The priests and staff are always ready to assist with rituals, answer questions, and guide visitors through the proper practices. Whether you are a regular visitor or a first-time guest, you will feel welcomed and at ease.

Clean and Well-Maintained:
Temple is impeccably clean and well-maintained, which adds to the overall positive experience. The temple grounds are tidy, and the facilities are regularly cleaned, making it a comfortable place to spend time in prayer or contemplation. The management ensures that everything is in order, which reflects the respect and devotion of those who care for the temple.

Convenient Location:
Located in Jogeshwari East, the temple is easily accessible by public transport and is well-known among locals. Despite being in a busy area, it retains a sense of tranquility that makes it a perfect escape for spiritual seekers.

Conclusion:
it is a gem for anyone looking to connect with their spirituality or simply find a peaceful place to reflect. Its serene environment, beautiful architecture, and welcoming community make it a standout place of worship in Mumbai. Whether you visit to offer prayers, meditate, or participate in religious ceremonies, you will leave feeling refreshed and spiritually uplifted. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: prathamesh kapde
featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Veludharan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jogeshwari Caves hewed during 6th century CE, is one of the finest specimen of Brahmanical rock-cut architecture and bears similarity with Elephanta (Cave no.1) and Dhumar lena (Cave no. 29) at Ellora. On plan, it consists of agra mandapa, mukha mandapa and garbhagriha. Vakataka and later Vakataka, influence can clearly be noticed in its architectural planning and sculptural execution. Some scholars believe that the caves were excavated under the patronage of Maurya of Konkan, Kalachuri (Traikutakas). Jogeshwari cave is adorned with a few beautiful sculptural representations of Lakulisa. Kalyansundarmurti, Shiv Parvati playing dyuta, Natraja, Ravananugraha, Makartornas, ayudhprushas, Dwarapalas etc.
It was declared as a protected monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India, vide gazette notification no. 2704A, dated 26.05. 1009

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Gajur
featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.
Weathered Carvings: Be prepared that many of the old carvings are heavily weathered. While their original splendor may be diminished, they still tell a story of a distant past.
Unique Temple Setup: The main sanctum is a must-see. The temple dedicated to Goddess Jogeshwari Mata is located in the basement. You will also find shrines for Lord Shiva in one corner and a more hidden shrine for Lord Hanuman in another.
East Gate Temple: If you enter or exit via the East Gate, you'll find a separate temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh.
Multiple Entrances: The caves are accessible via two main entrances, one on the East and one on the West.
📸 Pro-Tip: The Hidden Viewpoint
After exploring the basement shrine, make sure to ask a local for the way to the top of the caves. The journey offers a reward: a good panoramic view of the entire structure and surrounding area.
🕉️ Other Shrines Nearby
The complex holds several other important deities worth visiting:
There is a second dedicated temple to Lord Hanuman (ask a local for directions, as it might be slightly hidden).
Look for a temple housing Kal Bhairav and other deities on the other side of the complex.
⏱️ Essential Visiting Hours
Please note the specific timings for your visit:
The temple is closed during the afternoon.
It reopens in the evening at 4 PM.
Recommendation: Visit in the early morning or late evening to experience the temple and avoid the mid-day closure.
Overall: Jogeshwari Caves is a unique, spiritual, and historical experience. While the carvings are worn, the atmosphere and the ancient rock-cut architecture make this a worthwhile stop for anyone interested in Mumbai's pre-medieval history.

featured_reviews.name: Suresh Isave
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves feature beautiful carvings, though some aspects appear unfinished.  There's a large cave with the Jogeshwari Devi temple, and grand pillars are present.  However, the area doesn't seem well-maintained, and there's a noticeable unpleasant smell from plastic waste.  Parking is also an issue, as none is available close by. Entry is free.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves act as a haunting reminder of Mumbai's deep ancient roots, representing some of the earliest and most significant Hindu and Buddhist rock-cut architecture in the region. Stepping inside, one can still sense the majesty of the past through the massive pillars and the lingering spiritual aura of the central Shiva shrine. However, the site is in a heartbreaking state of decay, suffocated by encroaching slums and plagued by sewage seepage and piled-up debris that obscure its historical value. It is a heritage monument that is desperately crying out for comprehensive restoration and protection; without immediate intervention to clear the surroundings and preserve the crumbling rockwork, this archaeological treasure risks being lost entirely to urban neglect.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
The caves are located just off the Western Express Highway and are surrounded by heavy encroachments. Access is through a long flight of stairs that leads into the main hall of the cavern. Unfortunately, the site is in very poor condition—extremely unhygienic, poorly maintained, and the area smells terrible.

I would strongly advise against making a special trip, as you are likely to feel disappointed and even upset by the neglect and lack of care shown by the authorities and local people. The site remains open at all times with no entry gate or time restrictions, which further contributes to its deteriorated state.

featured_reviews.name: RuSo
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Jogeshwari Caves and it was a surprisingly powerful experience. One of the oldest rock-cut cave temples in India, the place has a raw, ancient energy that you can actually feel as you walk inside. The carvings dedicated to Lord Shiva, especially forms like Nataraja, are beautiful and carry a quiet intensity.

The caves are not very well maintained compared to places like Elephanta Caves, and there can be waterlogging and a bit of mess around, but that also adds to the untouched, authentic feel of the site.

If you enjoy history, architecture, or just want a peaceful spot away from the usual crowds, this place is worth a visit. A hidden gem in Mumbai that deserves more care and attention.
